plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to eliminate their risk.
Sell semiconductor ETFs (SMH, SMCI) to reduce sector concentration.
Trim the QQQI holding to 20% to address concentration and favor income.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by reducing high-risk assets.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained, increasing safety.
Expect lower volatility and a more stable portfolio.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on preserving capital with minimal drawdown. Expect a lower target return, around 1.5% per month, due to reduced risk and leverage. The primary goal is to protect equity from significant losses.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration and maintain income focus.
Sell leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to reduce overall risk.
Sell semiconductor holdings (SMH, SMCI) to diversify away from tech.
Buy XLF (Financials) to add diversification outside of tech.
This plan balances risk reduction with potential for growth.
A moderate cash buffer will be kept for flexibility.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding some diversification. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate, with a focus on protecting capital while seeking gains.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration while retaining some income.
Add to leveraged ETFs SOXL and MUU, increasing exposure to tech.
Sell underperforming semiconductor holdings SMH and SMCI.
Buy QCOM and AMD, focusing on strong scanner setups.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth mode targets approximately 4% per month by leaning into leverage and high-conviction tech names. It accepts higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the decay effects of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to remove volatility.
Sell high-beta semiconductor holdings (SMH, SMCI) to reduce risk.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to maximize income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over growth.
Leverage will be minimized to ensure capital preservation.
Expect consistent distributions, though NAV can still fluctuate.
income.read: This income-focused mode aims for stable monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It prioritizes income-generating assets like QQQI and minimizes risk by cutting leverage and high-beta single names. While distributions are prioritized, the Net Asset Value (NAV) can still decline in market downturns.
